title: Cloud First Development Strategy
definition: A development strategy that involves maintaining the primary version of the code on a cloud-based repository and pulling changes to local environments when necessary.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of cloud-first development as working primarily online. This means making changes and testing in the cloud, then pulling those changes to your local system when you're ready.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Cloud-first development involves maintaining the primary codebase on a cloud repository and using Git for version control. This allows for collaborative development and ensures that the latest code is always available.
difficulty_levels.expert: Cloud-first development is a shift in paradigm that emphasizes the cloud as the primary environment for code storage and development. It offers benefits such as enhanced collaboration, accessibility, and CI/CD opportunities. However, it also raises questions about data security and the role of local environments in the development process.

extra_fields.insight: The user discovered that after maintaining sanitized versions of their local system in a cloud repository, they could potentially work fully in the cloud environment and pull changes to local production copies when ready.
